summary: The fold: a note's content is a pure function of its .raw log. Its header states the property that matters most and that nothing else in the tree makes obvious — 'render is a fold, and the fold IS the merge': records sort by ts, tie-broken by a canonical-JSON compare specifically so git-union interleave order is irrelevant, then fold left through merge-by-id. Same operation for a same-branch append and a cross-branch git merge, so there is no separate merge algorithm to find or write. Per-field rules are documented in that header (title/summary/body last-writer-wins; aliases/invariants union; anchors union by path with hash/head updated only by records that carry them). It is a tolerant reader: structurally-invalid records, unknown ops and records from a newer major are skipped with a warning rather than erroring, and unknown fields are preserved into `extra` — which is what makes the raw format forward-compatible with fields older clients do not know.

It is a tolerant reader: structurally-invalid records, unknown ops and records from a newer major are skipped with a warning rather than erroring, and unknown fields are preserved into `extra` — which is what makes the raw format forward-compatible with fields older clients do not know. THE ALIAS UNION IS UNBOUNDED AND THAT IS A RECALL BUG (verified 2026-07-30, unfixed): aliases union with no cap, so a note's alias count grows with how many times it has been written, and per-write guidance cannot bound it. Measured on this repo — every individual alias write obeys the capture prompt's 6-10 rule (median 6 aliases / 20 words per put record, before AND after that guidance shipped), yet src/kb/search.ts's note reached 57 aliases across nine compliant writes (6 → 7 → 11 → 23 → 29 → 39 → 45 → 52 → 57). This matters because the name channel is zero-sum: hookNameNorm in search.ts divides title+aliases by their own token count, so an accumulating note steadily dilutes every alias it owns. Diagnose alias bloat here, not in the capture prompt — the agents are complying. A cap belongs at the union, where it stays a pure function of the log.

summary: The fold: a note's content is a pure function of its .raw log. Its header states the property that matters most and that nothing else in the tree makes obvious — 'render is a fold, and the fold IS the merge': records sort by ts, tie-broken by a canonical-JSON compare specifically so git-union interleave order is irrelevant, then fold left through merge-by-id. Same operation for a same-branch append and a cross-branch git merge, so there is no separate merge algorithm to find or write. Per-field rules are documented in that header (title/summary/body last-writer-wins; aliases/invariants union; anchors union by path with hash/head updated only by records that carry them). It is a tolerant reader: structurally-invalid records, unknown ops and records from a newer major are skipped with a warning rather than erroring, and unknown fields are preserved into `extra` — which is what makes the raw format forward-compatible with fields older clients do not know. ALIAS BLOAT IS DIAGNOSED HERE, NOT IN THE CAPTURE PROMPT. The alias union was unbounded until 2026-07-30, so a note's alias count grew with how many times it had been written and per-write guidance could not bound it: every individual write in this repo obeyed the prompt's 6-10 rule (median 6 aliases / 20 words per put record, before AND after that guidance shipped in v2.2.9), yet src/kb/search.ts's note reached 57 aliases across nine compliant writes. If you find a note with a bloated alias list, the agents were complying — look at the union, not at the writers. `capAliases` now caps it newest-first against a word budget (ALIAS_MAX_WORDS, the real currency because hookNameNorm divides the name channel by its own token count) with ALIAS_MAX as a secondary count guard and a 4-alias floor. Newest-first is deterministic but is NOT quality-ranked: it keeps whatever the most recent writers chose, which on a heavily-revised note can evict its best symptom keys — that trim rule, not the budget size, is the first thing to revisit if recall regresses. Nothing is ever lost: the fold is a pure function of the append-only log, so widening the constants and re-rendering restores every alias exactly.

'aliasesVerified' is added to PUT_KEYS purely so it is not dumped into note.extra; it carries no stored content of its own.
